subject: Barn Owl
fact: Barn owls can hunt in darkness by using extremely sensitive hearing.

subject: Great Horned Owl
fact: Great horned owls have feather tufts that look like ears but are not their actual ears.

subject: Eastern Screech-Owl
fact: Eastern screech-owls can hide well against tree bark because of their mottled feathers.

subject: Burrowing Owl
fact: Burrowing owls often live in underground burrows and may be active around dusk.

subject: Tawny Owl
fact: Tawny owls are woodland hunters with excellent night vision and hearing.

subject: Snowy Owl
fact: Snowy owls may hunt during daylight in Arctic summers where the sun stays up for long periods.

subject: Long-Eared Owl
fact: Long-eared owls have tall feather tufts and often rest quietly in dense trees during the day.

subject: Short-Eared Owl
fact: Short-eared owls often hunt low over open fields at dawn and dusk.

subject: Little Owl
fact: Little owls are small owls that may perch on posts while watching for prey.

subject: Nightjar
fact: Nightjars have wide mouths that help them catch flying insects.

subject: Nighthawk
fact: Nighthawks catch insects while flying and are most active around evening.

subject: Kakapo
fact: Kakapos are flightless parrots from New Zealand that are active mostly at night.

subject: Kiwi
fact: Kiwis use long beaks and sensitive nostrils to search for food on the forest floor.

subject: Tarsier
fact: Tarsiers have enormous eyes that help them see in low light.

subject: Aye-Aye
fact: Aye-ayes use a long middle finger to find insects hidden inside wood.

subject: Slow Loris
fact: Slow lorises are small primates with large eyes adapted for nighttime activity.

subject: Bushbaby
fact: Bushbabies can make powerful leaps between branches at night.

subject: Mouse Lemur
fact: Mouse lemurs are tiny nocturnal primates from Madagascar.

subject: Raccoon
fact: Raccoons use sensitive front paws to explore food and objects.

subject: Opossum
fact: Opossums are the only marsupials native to the United States and Canada.

subject: Skunk
fact: Skunks can spray a strong-smelling liquid when they feel threatened.

subject: Badger
fact: Badgers are strong diggers that often rest in underground burrows.

subject: Hedgehog
fact: Hedgehogs can curl into a tight ball to protect themselves with their spines.

subject: Porcupine
fact: Porcupines are covered with modified hairs called quills.

subject: Armadillo
fact: Many armadillos search for insects at night using a strong sense of smell.

subject: Fennec Fox
fact: Fennec foxes have huge ears that help them hear prey and release body heat.

subject: Red Fox
fact: Red foxes use their large ears to locate small animals hidden in grass or snow.

subject: Gray Fox
fact: Gray foxes are unusual canids because they can climb trees.

subject: Coyote
fact: Coyotes communicate with yips, barks, and howls.

subject: Bobcat
fact: Bobcats are stealthy cats that often hunt around dawn, dusk, and nighttime.

subject: Leopard
fact: Leopards are powerful climbers and often rest or store food in trees.

subject: Clouded Leopard
fact: Clouded leopards have long tails that help them balance while climbing.

subject: Black-Footed Cat
fact: Black-footed cats are small African wild cats that hunt mostly at night.

subject: Pallas's Cat
fact: Pallas's cats have thick fur and rounded ears that help them blend into rocky habitats.

subject: Binturong
fact: Binturongs use long prehensile tails to help grip branches.

subject: Civet
fact: Many civets are nocturnal mammals that forage for fruit and small animals.

subject: Genet
fact: Genets are agile nighttime hunters with long spotted bodies and ringed tails.

subject: Kinkajou
fact: Kinkajous use long tongues to reach fruit and nectar.

subject: Sugar Glider
fact: Sugar gliders can glide between trees using skin stretched between their legs.

subject: Flying Squirrel
fact: Flying squirrels glide from tree to tree using a membrane of skin between their limbs.

subject: Vampire Bat
fact: Vampire bats can detect warm spots on the skin of their prey.

subject: Fruit Bat
fact: Many fruit bats use their keen senses to find ripe fruit at night.

subject: Little Brown Bat
fact: Little brown bats use echolocation to catch insects in darkness.

subject: Greater Horseshoe Bat
fact: Horseshoe bats use a leaf-like nose structure to help focus echolocation calls.

subject: Flying Fox
fact: Flying foxes are large fruit bats with faces that resemble small foxes.

subject: Moth
fact: Many moths are active at night and use feathery antennae or scent to find mates.

subject: Firefly
fact: Fireflies make light with a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.

subject: Scorpion
fact: Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light because of chemicals in their outer covering.

subject: Tarantula
fact: Many tarantulas wait near burrows at night to catch insects and other small prey.

subject: Orb-Weaver Spider
fact: Many orb-weaver spiders build new circular webs during evening or nighttime.

subject: Praying Mantis
fact: Some praying mantises hunt insects at night near lights.

subject: Katydid
fact: Katydids often call after dark by rubbing parts of their wings together.

subject: Cricket
fact: Male crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together.

subject: Gecko
fact: Many geckos are active at night and can climb smooth surfaces with specialized toe pads.

subject: Tokay Gecko
fact: Tokay geckos are large nocturnal geckos known for their loud calls.

subject: Leopard Gecko
fact: Leopard geckos have movable eyelids and store fat in their tails.

subject: Ball Python
fact: Ball pythons are most active at night and may curl into a ball when frightened.

subject: Boa Constrictor
fact: Boa constrictors use heat-sensitive pits to help detect warm animals.

subject: Axolotl
fact: Axolotls are aquatic salamanders that keep their feathery external gills as adults.

subject: Cane Toad
fact: Cane toads often become active after sunset when temperatures are cooler.
